metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies when AI generated 'the vast majority' of a submission (e.g., agent-based or vibe coding).

evidence.quote: If you use Generative AI to write the vast majority of your submission (e.g., agent-based or vibe coding) then you **must document your use of AI** in your pull request.
Please include the service you used and/or model that generated the code.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named for AI-assisted code
domains.reasoning: The policy names code contributions and states a disclosure requirement (supervision level) when AI wrote the majority of a submission, but never states who is answerable for the resulting code beyond the general 'all code submissions go through review' statement, which is enforcement/process, not accountability.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: The document never discusses recorded meetings, notetaker bots, or discussion-capture tools.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use for docs/design assets/blogs
domains.reasoning: The 'Using AI' section is scoped explicitly to code submissions ('write the vast majority of your submission ... generated the code'); it does not mention documentation, blog posts, or design assets, and no other section addresses non-code content.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI-assisted moderation actions
domains.reasoning: No text discusses AI being used to triage, label, close, or otherwise moderate issues/PRs.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on AI use during code/PR review
domains.reasoning: 'All code submissions go through a rigorous review process regardless of the development workflow used' describes an existing human review process and does not state whether AI may be used to conduct that review, so it does not name AI-assisted review as a rule.

domains.suggested_improvement: no separate rule for agentic/autonomous repo interaction
domains.reasoning: 'Agent-based or vibe coding' is cited only as an example of a submission method subject to the code_contributions disclosure rule; it does not set an independent supervision level for an agent acting autonomously on the repository (opening PRs, commenting, merging, etc.).
No text in the file references environmental cost of AI tooling.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of server load or hardware cost from AI
domains.reasoning: No text references infrastructure strain, server load, or hardware financing related to AI.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on use of project data to train models
domains.reasoning: The file never discusses whether the project's own content, issues, or discussions may be used to train AI models.

unscoped_statements.quote: If you use Generative AI to write the vast majority of your submission (e.g., agent-based or vibe coding) then you must document your use of AI in your pull request.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The file addresses only one domain with any specificity: code contributions, where a disclosure requirement applies to majority-AI-generated submissions, but even there no accountability holder is named; all other eight domains (notetaker bots, content, moderation, review, autonomous, environmental, infrastructure, training data) are entirely unaddressed in this document.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
